**Lower rent survives the baseline comparison.** Six charts compare real asking rents with modeled travel and winter bills.

<p style="font-size:14px;color:#526270">Select a chart to open its full-size image.</p>

```{r prepare, include=FALSE}
if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "English_United States.utf8")
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
options(tinytex.install_packages = FALSE, scipen = 999)
rentals <- read.csv("data/rentals.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tariffs <- read.csv("data/tariffs.csv")
wages <- read.csv("data/wages.csv")
sources <- read.csv("data/sources.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rate <- setNames(tariffs$value, tariffs$parameter)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = knitr::is_html_output(), message = FALSE,
  warning = TRUE, dev = "png", dpi = 160, fig.show = "hold", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5,
  fig.path = file.path(normalizePath(tempdir(), winslash = "/"), "yerevan-chart-"),
  out.width = "100%")
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12, base_family = "sans") + theme(plot.margin = margin(8, 24, 8, 8)))
blue <- "#286C8E"
orange <- "#AF572E"
amd <- scales::label_number(scale = 0.001, suffix = "k", accuracy = 1)
```

## Where is rent cheaper?

```{r rent, fig.link='../figures/01-rent.png', fig.alt='Open full-size boxplots of observed asking rent distributions by district'}
districts <- rentals %>% group_by(district) %>% summarise(
  n = n(), rent = median(rent_amd), q1 = quantile(rent_amd, 0.25),
  q3 = quantile(rent_amd, 0.75), area = median(area_m2),
  km = median(round_trip_km), minutes = median(freeflow_minutes), .groups = "drop")
order <- districts$district[order(districts$rent)]
district_labels <- setNames(paste0(districts$district, "  ·  n=", districts$n,
  ifelse(districts$n < 10, "*", "")), districts$district)
rent_plot <- ggplot(rentals, aes(rent_amd, factor(district, levels = order))) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = district == "Kentron"), width = 0.55, outlier.size = 1.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = blue, "TRUE" = "#374151"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = district_labels) + scale_x_continuous(labels = amd) +
  labs(x = "Monthly asking rent (AMD)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Boxes: middle 50% of ads. Line: median. Whiskers: up to 1.5 box lengths beyond box edges.\nDots: beyond whiskers. Two rooms, 45–75 m², furniture advertised. *Fewer than 10 ads: read cautiously.")
rent_plot
ggsave("figures/01-rent.png", rent_plot, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 180)
```

<div class="takeaway">

**Kentron has the highest median asking rent.** Its median is `r format(districts$rent[districts$district == "Kentron"], big.mark = ",")` AMD, compared with `r format(min(districts$rent), big.mark = ",")`–`r format(max(districts$rent[districts$district != "Kentron"]), big.mark = ",")` AMD elsewhere in this sample. The boxes show overlapping distributions, so district alone does not determine a listing's price.

</div>

::: {=latex}
\newpage
:::

## How much longer is the commute?

```{r commute, fig.link='../figures/02-commute.png', fig.alt='Open full-size chart of modeled one-way commute minutes by district and mode'}
travel <- bind_rows(
  districts %>% mutate(mode = "Public transport", trip_minutes = km / 12 * 60 + 30),
  districts %>% mutate(mode = "Private car", trip_minutes = minutes * 1.5 + 10))
commute_pairs <- travel %>% select(district, mode, trip_minutes) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = trip_minutes)
commute_plot <- ggplot(travel, aes(trip_minutes / 2,
  factor(district, levels = order), color = mode, shape = mode)) +
  geom_segment(data = commute_pairs,
    aes(x = `Private car` / 2, xend = `Public transport` / 2,
        y = factor(district, levels = order), yend = factor(district, levels = order)), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#BAC6CE", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Private car" = blue, "Public transport" = "#657580"), name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Private car" = 16, "Public transport" = 17), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Modeled minutes per one-way journey", y = NULL,
       caption = "Each connecting line shows the difference between the two modeled travel modes.\nDestination: Republic Square. Transit: 12 km/h + 15 min per leg; car: 1.5 × free-flow + 5 min per leg.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
commute_plot
ggsave("figures/02-commute.png", commute_plot, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 180)
```

<div class="takeaway">

**Public transport takes longer in these modeled comparisons.** Longer connecting lines show a larger gap between the two modes. Kentron is closer to the shared destination. These are road-based scenarios—not timed journeys, live traffic, or actual bus routes.

</div>

::: {=latex}
\newpage
:::

## What does the monthly budget include?

```{r budgets, fig.link='../figures/03-budget.png', fig.alt='Open full-size chart of modeled rent, utility and transport components'}
days <- 22
commuters <- 1
wage <- wages$Value[wages$Year == 2025]
hourly <- wage / (22 * 8)
time_value <- hourly / 2
utilities <- 150 * rate["electric_day_low"] + 50 * rate["electric_night_low"] +
  100 * rate["gas_per_1000m3"] / 1000 + 8 * rate["water_per_m3"]
budgets <- travel %>% mutate(
  transport = ifelse(mode == "Public transport",
    commuters * pmin(2 * days * rate["fare_single"], rate["fare_30day"]),
    commuters * (km * days * 60 + 10000)),
  hours = trip_minutes * days * commuters / 60,
  direct = rent + utilities + transport,
  with_time = direct + hours * time_value)
central <- budgets %>% filter(district == "Kentron") %>%
  select(mode, central_direct = direct, central_hours = hours, central_total = with_time)
comparisons <- budgets %>% left_join(central, by = "mode") %>% mutate(
  saving = central_total - with_time, direct_difference = direct - central_direct,
  extra_hours = hours - central_hours)
components <- budgets %>% mutate(utilities = utilities) %>%
  select(district, mode, rent, utilities, transport) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(rent, utilities, transport), names_to = "component", values_to = "amd")
components$component <- factor(components$component, levels = c("transport", "utilities", "rent"))
budget_plot <- ggplot(components, aes(amd, factor(district, levels = order), fill = component)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) + facet_wrap(~mode, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(rent = "#AFC8D5", utilities = "#657580", transport = blue), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = amd) +
  labs(x = "Selected cash costs per month (AMD)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Rent + modeled electricity, gas, water and commuting. One commuter, 22 return-commute days.\nSame winter consumption in every district; heating is included once through gas.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
budget_plot
ggsave("figures/03-budget.png", budget_plot, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 180)
```

<div class="takeaway">

**Rent is the largest part of the selected budget.** Modeled winter utilities add `r format(round(utilities), big.mark = ",")` AMD everywhere. Public fares can be the same despite a longer journey; driving adds distance-dependent costs. Time is not a cash cost and is added in the next chart.

</div>

::: {=latex}
\newpage
:::

## How much saving remains after valuing time?

```{r savings, fig.link='../figures/04-saving.png', fig.alt='Open full-size waterfall showing how rent savings are reduced by added transport and valued time'}
noncentral <- comparisons %>% filter(district != "Kentron")
focus_district <- noncentral$district[which.min(noncentral$saving)]
central_transport <- budgets %>% filter(district == "Kentron") %>%
  select(mode, transport_kentron = transport)
focus <- noncentral %>% filter(district == focus_district) %>%
  left_join(central_transport, by = "mode") %>% mutate(
    rent_saved = districts$rent[districts$district == "Kentron"] - rent,
    transport_added = transport - transport_kentron, time_added = extra_hours * time_value)
waterfall <- focus %>% select(mode, rent_saved, transport_added, time_added, saving) %>%
  mutate(transport_added = -transport_added, time_added = -time_added) %>%
  pivot_longer(-mode, names_to = "step_name", values_to = "amount") %>%
  group_by(mode) %>% mutate(step = row_number(),
    end = ifelse(step == 4, amount, cumsum(amount)),
    start = ifelse(step %in% c(1, 4), 0, end - amount),
    kind = ifelse(step %in% c(1, 4), "Saving", "Added cost")) %>% ungroup()
saving_plot <- ggplot(waterfall) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#374151") +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = step - 0.32, xmax = step + 0.32,
    ymin = pmin(start, end), ymax = pmax(start, end), fill = kind)) +
  geom_segment(data = filter(waterfall, step < 4),
    aes(x = step + 0.32, xend = step + 0.68, y = end, yend = end), color = "#657580") +
  geom_text(aes(step, pmax(start, end), label = amd(amount)), vjust = -0.6, size = 3.8) +
  facet_wrap(~mode, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Saving" = blue, "Added cost" = orange), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4, labels = c("Rent\nsaved", "Extra\ntransport", "Extra\ntime", "Saving\nleft")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = amd, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.16))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Monthly saving relative to Kentron (AMD)",
       subtitle = paste("Focus:", focus_district, "— the smallest remaining baseline saving"),
       caption = "Blue: savings. Orange: extra costs. Equal utilities cancel in this comparison.\nTime is valued at half the gross hourly wage benchmark. These are modeled budgets, not observed bills.")
saving_plot
ggsave("figures/04-saving.png", saving_plot, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 180)
cheaper <- sum(noncentral$saving > 0)
```

<div class="takeaway">

**Even the most exposed baseline example retains a saving.** The waterfall follows `r focus_district`, selected because it contains the smallest remaining saving. All `r cheaper` district–mode examples remain cheaper than Kentron at about `r round(time_value)` AMD/hour for time. These results apply to the stated sample and assumptions.

</div>

::: {=latex}
\newpage
:::

## When can the answer change?

```{r stress, fig.link='../figures/05-sensitivity.png', fig.alt='Open full-size heatmap of savings under heavier winter and commuting assumptions'}
grid <- expand.grid(workers = c(1, 2), workdays = c(16, 22, 26),
                    fraction = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1), extra_gas = c(0, 75, 150))
scenarios <- merge(travel, grid, by = NULL) %>% mutate(
  fare = workers * pmin(2 * workdays * rate["fare_single"], rate["fare_30day"]),
  car = workers * (km * workdays * 60 + 10000),
  gas_extra = ifelse(district == "Kentron", 0, extra_gas * rate["gas_per_1000m3"] / 1000),
  total = rent + utilities + gas_extra + ifelse(mode == "Public transport", fare, car) +
    trip_minutes * workdays * workers / 60 * fraction * hourly)
scenario_central <- scenarios %>% filter(district == "Kentron") %>%
  select(mode, workers, workdays, fraction, extra_gas, reference = total)
scenarios <- scenarios %>% left_join(scenario_central,
  by = c("mode", "workers", "workdays", "fraction", "extra_gas")) %>%
  mutate(saving = reference - total)
stress_rows <- scenarios %>% filter(workers == 2, workdays == 26,
  extra_gas == 150, district != "Kentron")
stress_plot <- ggplot(stress_rows, aes(factor(fraction),
  factor(district, levels = order), fill = saving)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = round(saving / 1000)), size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~mode, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B65D34", mid = "#FAF9F5", high = "#78A4B8",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-150000, 150000), breaks = c(-150000, 0, 150000), labels = amd) +
  labs(x = "Time value as a fraction of the gross hourly benchmark", y = NULL, fill = "Saving",
       caption = "A stress example: 2 commuters, 26 days, +150 m³ gas outside Kentron.\nCells show AMD thousands saved; negative values mean more expensive. These are assumptions, not probabilities.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
stress_plot
ggsave("figures/05-sensitivity.png", stress_plot, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 180)
reversals <- sum(scenarios$saving < 0 & scenarios$district != "Kentron")
```

<div class="takeaway">

**More commuting and heating can erase the saving in some cases.** The chosen grid contains `r reversals` more-expensive cases. The chart shows one heavy-commuting winter example; it does not estimate how often households face those conditions. Two-car cases assume separate journeys and vehicles.

</div>

::: {=latex}
\newpage
:::

## When would the saving disappear?

```{r threshold, fig.link='../figures/06-break-even.png', fig.alt='Open full-size dotplot of twenty break-even time values and the gross wage benchmark'}
thresholds <- noncentral %>% mutate(
  break_even = ifelse(direct_difference < 0 & extra_hours > 0,
                     -direct_difference / extra_hours, NA_real_))
threshold_plot <- ggplot(thresholds, aes(break_even,
  factor(district, levels = order))) +
  geom_point(color = blue, size = 3.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = hourly, linetype = "dashed", color = orange, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~mode, nrow = 1) + scale_x_continuous(labels = amd) +
  labs(x = "Break-even value of commuting time (AMD/hour)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Each dot is a break-even threshold; below it, that district example remains cheaper.\nDashed line: gross wage benchmark. Other costs are held fixed; this is not a universal distance threshold.")
threshold_plot
ggsave("figures/06-break-even.png", threshold_plot, width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 180)
lowest_threshold <- min(thresholds$break_even, na.rm = TRUE)
```

<div class="takeaway">

**The answer depends on how you value extra time.** The lowest positive threshold is about `r format(round(lowest_threshold), big.mark = ",")` AMD/hour, above the `r format(round(hourly), big.mark = ",")` AMD/hour gross benchmark used here. This is a conditional calculation, and some district samples are small.

</div>

## What should a renter take from this?

In the baseline model, the rent saving is large enough to cover the selected extra costs. A renter should still compare a real quote with their own commute, heating needs and value of time. The stress chart shows why the conclusion should remain conditional.

The evidence does **not** support a blanket claim that cheaper noncentral housing always becomes more expensive. It also does not prove that every noncentral apartment is cheaper overall.

## Assumptions and sources

<details>
<summary>Read the household and travel assumptions</summary>

### The household example

Two adults, one commuter, 22 return-commute days per 30-day month. Winter consumption is assumed to be 150 daytime plus 50 nighttime kWh, 100 m³ gas and 8 m³ metered water. Equal consumption is used across districts. These are not observed bills.

Public transport uses the cheaper of single rides and one 30-day pass per commuter. Car costs assume 60 AMD/km plus 10,000 AMD monthly parking per commuter, excluding full vehicle ownership. Public time uses car-road distance at 12 km/h plus 15 minutes per leg; car time uses 1.5 times free-flow duration plus 5 minutes per leg. Neither is an observed peak journey or bus itinerary.

Time is valued at half of Armstat's 2025 national gross monthly wage divided by 176 assumed paid hours. Zero time value gives the direct cash-cost result. Longer-pass commitments and social discounts are outside the baseline.

### How the district budgets work

Each example combines its sample-median asking rent with median round-trip road inputs. Those medians may come from different apartments. Adding these components creates a modeled district budget—not the median of actual household bills. Kentron has its own nonzero commute to Republic Square.

Rent, modeled electricity/gas/water and commuting are included. Food, internet, building fees, moving costs, deposits and full car ownership are excluded. Heating is counted once through gas.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Read about the sample, statistics and checks</summary>

### Data and limitations

The four CSVs in `data/` are the complete inputs. `rentals.csv` is already cleaned: 276 native-AMD, two-room, 45–75 m² advertisements with furniture advertised and usable route inputs. The original 949-record extraction, exclusion evidence and route replies are preserved in `_archive/previous-version/`.

This is one agency's catalogue, retrieved on 5 November 2026—not random sampling or completed leases. Availability and last price-update dates are unverified. Condition and building information are incomplete, and district labels/coordinates may be approximate. These comparisons are not quality-adjusted or causal. Outside Kentron is not outside the Yerevan municipality; Abovyan and Masis are not compared.

Boxes show listing quartiles, and whiskers extend to values within 1.5 box lengths; dots show values beyond them. These are not confidence intervals. We do not manufacture population p-values from convenience advertisements or scenario rows. The graphs communicate descriptive statistics and sensitivity to assumptions.

The original broader checks included faster/slower travel, transfers, a narrower size band and alternative aggregation. Their evidence remains archived; the simplified report retains the same primary sample, baseline calculations and full household/heating/time grid.

```{r checks, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(nrow(rentals) == 276, !anyDuplicated(rentals$listing_id))
stopifnot(all(rentals$rooms == 2), all(between(rentals$area_m2, 45, 75)))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(utilities), 24769.36)))
stopifnot(all(budgets$direct == budgets$rent + utilities + budgets$transport))
stopifnot(all(abs(noncentral$direct_difference +
  noncentral$extra_hours * thresholds$break_even) < 0.000001))
```
